questions.question: Do school buses have ABS?

options.text: No, they never have ABS.
Only in cold climates.
Some may have ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Some may have ABS.
questions.explanation: Most commercial vehicles made after 1998 or 1999 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS). Many older buses also have ABS.

questions.question: What should students do when leaving a bus?

options.text: Stay seated until the driver tells them to exit.
Stand up and walk to the door while the bus is moving.
Exit and stand next to the bus until it leaves.
Jump down from the top step.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay seated until the driver tells them to exit.
questions.explanation: Students must stay seated until the driver tells them to exit. After leaving, they should walk at least 10 feet away from the bus to a place where the driver can see them.

questions.question: If a student drops something while walking to the bus, what should they do?

options.text: Stop and pick it up.
Ask another student to pick it up.
Ask the driver to pick it up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask the driver to pick it up.
questions.explanation: If a student tries to pick up a dropped item, the driver may not see them. This is dangerous. Instead, the student should move to a safe place away from the bus, get the driver's attention, and ask the driver to get the item.

questions.question: If a student drops something while walking to the bus, what should they do?

options.text: Stop and pick it up.
Ask another student to pick it up.
Ask the driver to pick it up.
Leave it and walk away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask the driver to pick it up.
questions.explanation: It is dangerous for students to pick up dropped items because the driver may not see them at that moment. Students should move away from the bus's danger zones, get the driver's attention, and ask the driver to get the item.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on the expressway during the skills test?

options.text: Change lanes often.
Use your mirrors to check traffic.
Drive on the left side of the lane.
Drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors to check traffic.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, you may drive on an expressway. Stay in the proper lane, keep safe distance from other cars, and follow the speed limit. Always check your mirrors and look around for other traffic.

questions.question: What will the examiner grade you on during the driving test?

options.text: How well you speak.
How fast you reach your destination.
Your overall driving behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your overall driving behavior.
questions.explanation: The examiner will grade you on specific driving maneuvers and your general driving behavior. You must drive safely, obey all traffic signs and laws, and not cause an accident or get a ticket.

questions.question: What should the driver do while students load and unload?

options.text: Read a book.
Watch the students and the loading process.
Talk to other bus drivers.
Listen to the radio.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the students and the loading process.
questions.explanation: The driver must watch students as they enter and exit the bus. Make sure no one gets caught in the door or handrails. Check that students move far enough away from the bus after they exit.

questions.question: Where are the blind spots on the left and right flat mirrors?

options.text: Directly below the mirrors
In the middle of the mirrors
Above the mirrors
To the left of the mirrors

questions.correctAnswerText: Directly below the mirrors
questions.explanation: Blind spots exist directly below each outside flat mirror and in front of it. There is also a blind spot directly behind the rear bumper.

questions.question: When must a school bus be evacuated?

options.text: When the bus stalls in winter weather.
When the air conditioning breaks.
When there is danger of a collision.
When students feel sick.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is danger of a collision.
questions.explanation: Students should usually stay on the bus during emergencies. Evacuate only if the bus is on railroad tracks, on fire, has a fuel leak, or if there is danger of a collision.

questions.question: What do crossover mirrors help the driver see?

options.text: The danger zones in front of the bus.
The rear bumper.
The left side of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: The danger zones in front of the bus.
questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors show the driver the danger zones directly in front of the bus. They also show the danger zones on the left and right sides of the bus, from the front bumper to the service door.

questions.question: If a school bus needs to be evacuated, what should passengers do?

options.text: Always exit through the rear door.
Use the safest exit.
Always exit through the front door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the safest exit.
questions.explanation: When evacuating a school bus, the driver must quickly decide which exit is safest for all passengers to use.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, what should you check about the pedals?

options.text: The pedal surface has been smoothed out.
The gas pedal sticks.
Nothing blocks the pedals.
There is something under the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Nothing blocks the pedals.
questions.explanation: Check that nothing is under or around the pedals that prevents them from working. Make sure the pedals move freely and are in good working condition.

questions.question: When exiting your vehicle, what must you do?

options.text: Keep four points of contact with the vehicle.
Face the road before you finish exiting.
Face away from the vehicle.
Face the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Face the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always face the vehicle when exiting. Keep three points of contact with the vehicle at all times. On a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly will fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: What is an encroachment during a basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: Putting the vehicle in neutral and setting the parking brake.
The vehicle touching a boundary line.
Completing an exercise correctly.
Trying to bribe the examiner.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle touching a boundary line.
questions.explanation: An encroachment happens when any part of your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line during an exercise. Each encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: What should a properly adjusted outside convex mirror let you see?

options.text: The entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts.
The front of the bus.
The rear door of the bus.
The top of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: The entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts.
questions.explanation: Outside convex mirrors should be adjusted so you can see at least one traffic lane on each side of the bus, the entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts, and where the front of each rear tire touches the ground.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, which is NOT required?

options.text: Show that the oil pressure gauge works.
Show that the oil pressure warning light turns off, or the gauge shows normal pressure.
Show that the oil temperature gauge rises to normal operating temperature, if equipped.
Show that the oil pressure gauge comes on when brakes are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that the oil pressure gauge comes on when brakes are used.
questions.explanation: Check that the oil pressure gauge works and shows normal pressure, or that the warning light turns off. If equipped, the oil temperature gauge should gradually rise to normal operating temperature. The oil pressure gauge does not come on when brakes are used.

questions.question: If your bus's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops working, what happens?

options.text: You will have no brakes.
The brakes will respond more slowly.
You will still have normal braking power.
You should not brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will still have normal braking power.
questions.explanation: If the ABS stops working, your vehicle will still have normal braking power. Continue to drive and brake normally.

questions.question: How far behind the bus should a driver see with properly adjusted outside mirrors?

options.text: One bus length
Two bus lengths
Three bus lengths
Four bus lengths

questions.correctAnswerText: Four bus lengths
questions.explanation: The left and right side mirrors on a school bus should be adjusted so the driver can see 200 feet (about four bus lengths) behind the bus.

questions.question: How long before a school bus stop should the bus's lights be turned on?

options.text: 2 to 4 seconds
5 to 10 seconds
45 seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: 5 to 10 seconds
questions.explanation: Turn on the flashing amber warning lights at least 200 feet (about 5 to 10 seconds) before stopping, unless state law requires something different.

questions.question: If you cannot find a student after they exit the bus, what should you do?

options.text: Secure the bus and look for the student.
Assume the student got off safely.
Walk to the back of the bus to see if they got back on.
Ask another student if they've seen them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the bus and look for the student.
questions.explanation: If you cannot find a student after they exit, secure the bus and check around and under the bus for the missing student.
